title: Lathe tool orientation numbers depend on the turret side: PathPilot (rear tool, X+ toward the tool) numbers a standard OD tool 3, not 2

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found in M5's review of #640 (#630), which reads the LinuxCNC 1-9 orientation chart in its front-tool-lathe frame: standard OD tool = 2, tip offset (-X, -Z) from the nose centre.

**Evidence (contributor's Tormach PathPilot Hub 8L conversational samples, used as behaviour reference only):**
- `facing.nc`: a standard OD turning tool, "Tool on X+ side", is **Tool Orientation = 3**. It faces to centre with no complaint, while #640's fit table refuses 3 for facing.
- The OD threading sample wants orientation **8** where #640's table reads an OD thread tip as 6, (-X, 0).
- The chamfer refusals list [1,5,6] / [2,6,7] while the tool was 3 (to be reconciled).

**Reading:** the chart's numbers are drawn in a screen frame. On a rear-tool lathe the frame is mirrored in X: 1↔4, 2↔3, 6↔8, and 5, 7, 9 are unchanged. The physical tip offset of an OD tool is the same (-X, -Z) in machine coordinates either way. Only the **number** changes. So a PathPilot user who enters 3 (their tool table's number) gets the (+X, -Z) offset in #640: posted 2r wrong on diameter, and refused on facing.

**Expected:**
- A machine states its turret side (front or rear).
- The orientation number is read in that machine's frame, so built-in Lathe (front) 2 and Tormach 8L/15L (rear) 3 both mean the standard OD tool.
- Defaults follow the frame: OD insert 2 or 3, boring bar 3 or 2.
- The fit rule and the post's `ORIENTATION q` note use the machine's numbers.
- #641's blade corners (1/2/6) get the same treatment.

**Done means:**
- the three PathPilot data points above reproduce: a facing with 3 on a rear machine passes, an OD thread asks for 8, and the chamfer sets match;
- front-lathe behaviour and goldens are unchanged;
- a rear-machine golden is pinned.

**Blocks** #626 (PathPilot lathe post) and the Tormach lathe machines from relying on orientation numbers. Related: #630/#640, #641/#644, #647.

title: Lathe travel check judges world X, not the turning radius or the posted control point

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while widening the built-in Lathe's X floor for #630 (PR #640).

**Today:** the machine travel check compares each move's world X with the lathe's X band. The turning kernels put their radius on the **Y** meridian (a cached facing path is (0, y, z)), so on those paths the X band never sees the turning radius, whether nose centre or control point. A lathe X over-travel along the Y meridian is never judged by the stroke check. (Thread arcs in XY *are* seen, which is how #631 surfaced.) It also judges the cache (nose centre), not the posted control point that #640 now writes.

**Expected:** for lathe machines, the stroke check judges the **posted** position: the radius on the path's meridian (X or Y, the same way `nose_tip::control_point_path` reads it), shifted to the control point, against the X band; Z against the Z band. An over-travel is refused by name.

**Done means:** a facing path on the Y meridian that runs past the X floor is refused by name. A control point (not the nose centre) at the band edge decides it. Existing lathe goldens and suites stay green.

Related: #630/#640 (control point), #631/#643 (spindle-axis arcs).

title: Lathe grooving/parting: blades post the centre of the width, but a blade is touched off on a corner - groove Z off by width/2

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while fixing #630 (PR #640). It is the same class of bug as the nose-centre one.

**Today:** grooving and parting toolpaths post the blade's width-centre as the controlled point. A grooving or parting blade is touched off on a **corner** (LinuxCNC Lathe User Information §4.2), so with normal touch-off a groove lands **width/2 off in Z** and a part-off happens width/2 from where it was asked.

**Expected:** grooving and parting tools carry a reference corner (which side was touched off, as an orientation like #630's), and the shared CL→control-point conversion (`crates/post/src/post/nose_tip.rs`) shifts the blade path by width/2 (plus any corner radius) to that corner. A cut the corner can't reach is refused by name.

**Done means:** a 3 mm groove at Z-10 (centre) posts the touched-off corner at Z-8.5 or Z-11.5 per the reference side; a part-off at Z-20 cuts the part to length; existing groove/part goldens are regenerated with the shift explained.

Verify first: confirm on the engine's groove CL which point it emits (width centre vs a corner) before changing anything. If it already emits a corner, close this as not-a-bug.

title: M7.3: carried stock (the two-sided Body) on the field engine - prerequisite for #586/#589

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while working #586 (M7.3 3/6). Part of #26.

**Why #586 can't finish as a seam move:** every app stock *holder* is either a plain grid or the **carried `Body`** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry.rs`). `Body` stores the stock carried between setups as **two-sided columns**: `pub dex: Dexel` plus a per-column floor (`on_floor` / `on_mesh`). It supports the setup-change transforms that `LatticeTurn` makes exact on a lattice: XY quarter turns, Z flips and mirrors (`carry`, `deviate`'s Z-mirror via `Dexel::from_grid`, `display()`).

The app also **mutates** it as a column store:
- `simulate(&mut body.dex, ..)` in `rest/across.rs` and `rest.rs`;
- `stock_sim_carry`'s clip loop writing `dex.lower(..)`;
- `Held::Plain(Dexel)` / `Held::Carried(Body)` and `dex_mut()`.

Swapping `Dexel` for `Stock` there is a **data-model change**: carried stock on the field engine.

**Open design questions:**
1. **Representation:** the field engine holds a solid as a narrow-band SDF plus cut layers. Carrying it is a rigid transform of the field (a re-sample, or a transformed query frame) rather than a lattice permutation. Is a transformed query frame (no re-sample) exact enough for the verdicts?
2. **Floors:** a flipped part's floor is the former top. The field is a closed solid, so it has no separate floor, but "a column cut through" needs an equivalent read.
3. **Clipping** to a later setup's own stock: a field intersection (max of SDFs) replaces `lower`.
4. **Equivalence:** a heavy-lane agreement test of the carried verdicts (`setup_carry`, `rest_across_setups`, `carried_verify`) on both engines, like `stock_engine_agreement`.

**Done means:** `stock_sim_carry`, `rest`, `rest/across` and the operation priors hold carried stock as `Stock`. A field-engine carry passes the same carried-stock suites, plus an agreement lane against the column carry. #586 can then close. This is a prerequisite of #589.

Related: #26, #585 (PR #595), #586, #589, #633 (PR #636, the field block speed fix this depends on).

title: Field stock engine is ~300x slower than the column engine on a large box (blocks M7.3 retirement)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found in the review of PR #625 (#588, the `camcraft-sim` CLI onto the field engine), 2026-11-09. **This blocks #589**, the column engine's retirement.

**The measurement** (release build, same program and box):

| Engine | `drill_plate.cl`, box -60..60 × -60..60 × -25..0, default cell 0.375 mm (320 × 320) |
|---|---|
| column (old CLI) | ~0.23 s |
| field (#625) | **~79 s** |

That is about **300× slower**. The output is byte-identical, so it's speed only. #26's heavy agreement lane (`stock_field_cost`) reports 0.25-12 ms/move on the golden programs at its own 0.5 mm lattice. A drill program on a large box at the CLI's auto cell is much worse, probably from the field's per-cell march over a 320² lattice for every plunge, or its build cost.

**Why it matters:** #586, #587 and #589 move the app's carried, rest and prior stock and the motion generators onto the field. If those paths see similar ratios, retiring the column engine would make generation and post-time verification far slower. That's a usability regression the agreement suite can't catch, because it measures verdicts, not time.

**Expected:**
1. **Profile** the field engine on this case and name where the time goes: build, per-move cut, or the final `columns()` read-out.
2. **Fix or bound it:** a field-arm auto cell coarser than the column's where the verdict allows, batched cuts, or a faster read-out. Then state a **wall-time budget** in a heavy-lane test, e.g. "a golden program on a 120 mm box completes within N× the column engine", so the regression can't come back silently.
3. **Until then,** #586, #587 and #589 should not land on the field for interactive paths, and #625's CLI notes the cost in `--help`.

**Done means:** the drill_plate case and the golden programs run within a stated budget relative to the column engine, pinned by a heavy-lane timing test.

Related: #26, #584 (the per-brick law exists and holds, but it bounds work per brick, not total wall time), #585, #588 / PR #625, #589.

title: Lathe facing: the first move after a tool call is a feed with no rapid approach; each pass rapids out dragging across the face

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found in the #626 lathe investigation; shared by Fanuc Lathe and PathPilot output.

**Today:**
- **No rapid approach:** `crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs:205-209` starts a PathBuilder at `(rho_clear, clearance)` but never emits a move there. The first posted move is a **feed** to `(rho_clear, s + r)` from wherever the turret parked (`G01 X28 Z1.8 F0.0508`). That is an unplanned, unchecked path.
- **Dragging retract:** each pass ends with a rapid back out radially at the Z just cut (`face.rs:219-221`), so the nose drags across the fresh face.

**Expected:** a rapid to the clearance point before the first plunge, and a small Z lift (e.g. +0.2 mm) before the radial rapid out.

**Done means:** facing goldens show `G0` to clearance, then the feed in, and each retract lifts Z first.

title: P0: lathe posts output the insert's nose-centre path with G40 - turned diameters 2r oversize, faces r long

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Safety or crash: wrong output, gouge, data loss

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while building a PathPilot Hub kit for PR #626, then confirmed on upstream/main (66791aa6) with the Fanuc Lathe post.

**Today:**
- **The CL is the nose-circle centre:** `crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs:2-5` ("the CL point is the insert nose CIRCLE'S CENTER, held at station + nose_radius"); `prof.rs` and `profile.rs` follow the same law.
- **The posts write it raw:** `fanuc-lathe.cps` (header l.25-27) writes it with `G40` and refuses G41/G42 (l.274-282). `toolCr` only feeds the tool comment. No nose-centre → tip conversion exists anywhere in `crates/post`.
- **Kit numbers (Ø19.05 mm finish, r = 0.8 mm insert):** the Fanuc finish posts `G01 X20.65` (= 19.05 + 2r), and the last face pass is `Z0.8` for a face at Z0. PathPilot (#626) posts the same: X0.813 for Ø0.750. The golden `facing.nc` carries a "finish envelope … 0.8000 mm gouge" comment.
- **What the controls expect:** with G40, the controlled point is the imaginary tool tip from touch-off (LinuxCNC Lathe User Information §7.1, "tangent to the tool tip diameter, as defined when you touch off"; Fanuc's usual practice is the same). So with normal touch-off, ODs come out **2r oversize** and faces **r long**, and tapers and radii are distorted. Every lathe post is affected.

**Expected:** pick one of two shared fixes in the engine/post contract, not a per-post patch.
- **(a)** Turning inserts carry a tool orientation (tip direction, as Fanuc T-tip / LinuxCNC Q), and the CL-to-post layer shifts the nose centre to the imaginary tip for that orientation (e.g. an OD tool cutting toward the chuck: tip = centre − r in radius X and − r in Z).
- **(b)** Emit G41/G42 with the tip number and the true profile.

Either way, regenerate the Fanuc Lathe and PathPilot lathe goldens.

**Done means:** a finish to Ø19.05 posts X19.05 (or the comp-on profile), a face at Z0 posts Z0, a taper and a radius post exactly, and tests pin each tool orientation.

Reference pending: the contributor is posting PathPilot conversational **OD and ID chamfers** with "Tool radius compensation is used" (8L Hub). They will show how PathPilot writes nose comp (G41/G42 placement, part edge vs nose centre). They are syntax reference only.

Related: #626, #612.

title: P0: lathe threads are always cut left-hand (passes run +Z under M3; no hand parameter; posts drop the arc sense)

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Safety or crash: wrong output, gouge, data loss

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while building a PathPilot Hub kit for PR #626, then confirmed on upstream/main (66791aa6) with the Fanuc Lathe post.

**Today:**
- **No hand parameter:** there is no thread hand or feed direction anywhere: `ThreadParams` (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs:64-78`), `OpParams::Threading` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:2292-2304`), and the turning tool (no orientation).
- **The engine always cuts toward +Z:** passes run from the lowest station upward (`thread.rs:229-247`, `push_arc(..., true)`), and `Frame::about` forces the axis up (`profile.rs:66`), so every thread runs away from the chuck.
- **The posts drop the hand:** the CL's arc sense (ccw) describes a right-hand helix, but `fanuc-lathe.cps` `threadHalfTurn` (~l.498-517) throws it away and writes `G32 Z… F<lead>` under `M03` ("M03 always: the stream carries no spindle sense", l.61). M3 while feeding toward +Z (away from the chuck) cuts a **left-hand** thread.
- **Baked into the golden:** `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` (M03, start Z8, `G76 … Z14`).
- **Nothing catches it:** the thread verdict judges only the meridian, so a left-hand thread on a part drawn right-hand passes silently. That is wrong output by the Prime Directive.

**Expected:**
1. **Hand parameter:** Threading carries a `hand` (RH default) and possibly a feed direction (toward or away from the chuck).
2. **Engine:** the default cut is toward the chuck (start at the top station, descend, arcs `ccw=false`), and the `ThreadCycle` record carries the hand.
3. **Posts:** every lathe post (Fanuc Lathe, the PathPilot lathe post in #626) derives the hand from the arc sense plus the Z direction and writes M03 when it matches, otherwise M04 (or refuses by name). The hand is never dropped.
4. **Goldens:** `thread_g76.nc` and the G32/G33 goldens are regenerated.

**Done means:** an RH external thread posts toward the chuck under M3 on both lathe posts; an LH thread posts M4 or the opposite direction; tests pin hand × spindle × Z direction.

Reference pending: the contributor is posting a PathPilot conversational **external** 8-32 thread (8L Hub) showing the Z direction PathPilot's G76 uses for an RH OD thread. It is syntax reference only.

Related: #626, #612.

title: Post: a Tormach PathPilot lathe dialect (LinuxCNC G7/G8, one-block G76, G33)

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Raised by the contributor (2026-11-09) while planning Hub runs for the threading stack (#516 → #517 → #518 → #468). CamCraft's only lathe post is `fanuc-lathe.cps`. A Tormach lathe runs PathPilot, which is LinuxCNC, so Fanuc lathe output does not run on it:
- **Threading:** LinuxCNC's `G76` is one block (`G76 P Z I J K Q H E L`), not Fanuc's two-block `G76`. A spindle-synchronised pass is `G33` (or `G33.1` for a rigid tap). `G32` is not a thread move there.
- **Diameter mode:** the program states `G7` (diameter) or `G8` (radius). Plane `G18`.
- **Tool calls:** the `T0101`-style tool and offset words, and Tormach's tool-change conventions.
- **Retracts:** safe retract and home follow the mill post's PathPilot conventions (`G53` / `G30` where Tormach supports them on the lathe).

**Expected:** `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`, a PathPilot lathe dialect.
- **Sources:** specced from LinuxCNC's published G-code reference (lathe `G7`/`G8`, `G33`, `G76`) and Tormach's public PathPilot lathe documentation. Clean-room, recorded in the decision file.
- **Coverage:** facing, turning, grooving, drilling on centre, and threading (LinuxCNC `G76` and `G33` passes, including the #516 infeed and #518 repeat-pass features).
- **Goldens:** turning, threading and drilling goldens, with an inch and a mm program each.

**Done means:** the post is selectable on the Tormach lathes, conformance and golden tests pass, the threading output matches LinuxCNC's `G76` and `G33` syntax, and the contributor runs a turning and a threading program in PathPilot Hub's 8L or 15L simulator.

Related: the Tormach 8L/15L machines (companion issue); #516, #517, #518, #468.
